answer: Require each agent to lock a deposit before it can trade, and slash that deposit when peers prove it cheated. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but creating a thousand means locking a thousand deposits, so a sybil flood stops paying for itself. Think of trust like marble: it is carved slowly, one verified deal at a time, and a single bad trade chips it. An attacker who copies the same pitch across fake accounts leaves an echo that honest traders learn to spot, while real history moves at a glacier pace that cannot be faked overnight.
